lines.japanese: 帰路。
lines.english: On the way home.

lines.japanese: 嫌味な高層建築の窓明かりを背負って歩きながら、僕は≪召喚≫される直前の記憶を探っていた。
lines.english: As I walked with the garish glow of high-rise windows at my back, I searched my memory for the moments immediately preceding my Summoning.

lines.japanese: だけど思いだせない。
lines.english: But I could not remember.

lines.japanese: 「直前」よりも更に前のことなら覚えてる。
lines.english: I could remember what had happened before “immediately before.”

lines.japanese: せっかく渡来さんとの約束があったのに、高内さんが卒業文集の打ち合わせを始めるって言うものだから、僕は仕方なく教室で彼女を待っていたんだ。
lines.english: I had plans with Watarai, but Takauchi said she was going to begin the meeting about our graduation anthology, so I had no choice but to wait for her in the classroom.

lines.japanese: だけど高内さんは予定の時間より大幅に遅れてやって来て、悪びれもせず──
lines.english: But Takauchi showed up way past the time we'd agreed on and didn't even act sorry—

lines.japanese: ──あ！　そうだ、いいんだ。それは僕が集合場所を間違えていたせいだったんだ、彼女は悪くない。
lines.english: —Ah! No, that was all right. I had mistaken the meeting place. She had done nothing wrong.

lines.japanese: そのあと随分と一方的な要求を突きつけられもしたけど、そう、それは僕の落ち度だったから仕方ないんだ。それで……
lines.english: She'd made some pretty one-sided demands after that too, but, well, that was my fault, so what could I do? And then...

lines.japanese: ええーっと、それで……。
lines.english: Let's see. And then...

lines.japanese: そのあとだ。そこからが思いだせない。
lines.english: That was where it ended. Everything after that was gone.

lines.japanese: ううーん……。
lines.english: Hmm...

lines.japanese: グロリアス・マテリアルの副作用なのか、しばしば召喚術の弊害でこういう事態に陥ることはあった。
lines.english: Perhaps it was a side effect of the Glorious Material. The adverse consequences of the Summoning Art had often left me in situations like this.

lines.japanese: 僕はまだお酒に酔うという感覚を知らないけど、飲みすぎたお父さんが知らないあいだに家へ帰りついていたっていう、ありがちな笑い話みたいだ。
lines.english: I had yet to experience drunkenness myself, but it sounded like the stock joke about a father who drinks too much and somehow makes it home with no memory of getting there.

lines.japanese: 人間にも帰巣本能ってあるんだろうなあ。
lines.english: Maybe people have a homing instinct too.

lines.japanese: 煙草屋『ときつる』の明かりが見えたとき、昨日の朝あの小さなガラス張りの小窓から声をかけてくれた同級生のことが思いだされた。
lines.english: When the light of the Tokitsuru tobacco shop came into view, I remembered the classmate who had spoken to me yesterday morning through its little glass-fronted window.

lines.japanese: にわかに気の引きしまる思いで、僕は頭を起こした。空いている方の手を、意味もなくポケットへ突っこんでみる。
lines.english: I straightened at once, suddenly feeling the need to compose myself. For no particular reason, I thrust my free hand into my pocket.

lines.japanese: 山科さんはどうして昨日・今日と欠席だったんだろう。ちょっと聞いてみようかな。でもテストを休むぐらいの事情があるんだから、こんな時間に店番してるはずはないか。じゃあいいや。でもいたらどうしよう。
lines.english: Why had Yamashina been absent yesterday and today? Maybe I'd ask her. But if something made her miss a test, she probably wouldn't be minding the shop at this hour. Okay, forget it. But what if she was there?

lines.japanese: 正直に言えば、僕は緊張しているんだろう。萎縮と言ってもいいかもしれない。
lines.english: In truth, I was nervous. Intimidated might have been the better word.

lines.japanese: でも行こう。
lines.english: Still, I'll go.

lines.japanese: “６：クラスに友達をつくる”
lines.english: “6. Make a friend in class.”

lines.japanese: 彼女に卒業文集制作の手伝いをしてもらおう。
lines.english: I would ask her to help with the graduation anthology.

lines.japanese: 深呼吸。なんだか急に喉がいがらんだようで、いくつか咳払いをした。
lines.english: A deep breath. My throat had abruptly turned scratchy, and I cleared it several times.

lines.japanese: いよいよ僕の足は煙草屋へ近づいてゆき、神経質に唇を湿らせながら、はてさて第一声は「どーも」か「うっす」か「こんばんは」かと決めかねているうちに──
lines.english: The tobacco shop drew closer and closer as I wet my lips nervously, unable to decide whether to open with “Hey there,” “Yo,” or “Good evening”—

lines.japanese: ──無人の店内が、視野に入った。
lines.english: —the empty shop came into view.

lines.japanese: 無人。
lines.english: Empty.

lines.japanese: なあんだ。僕は脱力して無意識に安堵の溜息を漏らしたが、しかし、いざ店の前を通りすぎようというときには、未練がましくあの小さなガラス張りのカウンターから店の中をうかがったりもした。
lines.english: Oh. I sagged and let out an unconscious sigh of relief. Yet when the moment came to walk past, I could not resist one lingering glance into the shop through that small glass-fronted counter.

lines.japanese: 簡素な丸椅子に主はないが、その後ろの灯油ストーブは煌々と熱線色に照りあがっていた。エレキギターの低音が際立つハードロックなＢＧＭは、煙草のカートン箱が点在する和風の小部屋で遠慮がちに暴れていた。
lines.english: The plain round stool had no occupant, though the kerosene heater behind it blazed orange with radiant heat. Hard rock with a prominent low electric-guitar line rioted with curious restraint through the little Japanese room, among scattered cartons of cigarettes.

lines.japanese: あ、この曲どこかで……。
lines.english: Wait. I had heard this song somewhere...

lines.japanese: 聴きおぼえのあるメロディラインに惹かれていると、小部屋の奥の障子戸がすーっと開いた。
lines.english: As the familiar melodic line drew me in, the paper-screen door at the back of the room slid quietly open.

lines.japanese: 「いらっしゃ……あ」
lines.english: “Welco—oh.”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 見てるだけでもポカポカ温まりそうな炬燵と畳の茶の間から、煙草屋の娘が顔を覗かせた。僕は思わず逃げそうになったけど、もちろん逃げる理由なんて何もないんだから留まって軽く頭を下げた。
lines.english: The tobacco-shop girl peered out from a straw-matted sitting room with a heated table that seemed to warm me just to look at it. I nearly fled on instinct, but of course I had no reason to flee. I remained where I was and bowed lightly.

lines.japanese: 山科さんはにっこり微笑みながらサンダルを履いて、たぶん「おかえり」とか「おつかれ」とか、そんなような短い挨拶を一言発した。音楽に呑まれてよく聞こえなかったけど。
lines.english: Yamashina smiled, slipped into her sandals, and offered some brief greeting—perhaps “welcome home,” perhaps “long day?” The music swallowed it before I could make it out.

lines.japanese: 土間に下りた彼女はまずラジカセを止め、それから白木のサンダルをかろん、かろんと鳴らしてカウンターまでやって来た。
lines.english: Once she had stepped down into the earthen-floored entryway, she first stopped the stereo. Then she came to the counter, her pale wooden sandals knocking softly with every step.

lines.japanese: 「学生服のお客さんにはお売りできませんよ」
lines.english: “We don't sell to customers in school uniforms.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「あ……ああ、そうか、ここ煙草屋だっけ」
lines.english: “Oh... right. This is a tobacco shop.”

lines.japanese: 呆けていた僕がつい間抜けなことを口にすると、山科さんはゆっくり首を左右に巡らせ、据え付けの棚に並んだ有名無名の銘柄を見回した。
lines.english: Still dazed, I blurted out something stupid. Yamashina slowly turned her head from side to side and looked over the famous and not-so-famous brands lined up on the built-in shelves.

lines.japanese: それから丸椅子へ静かに腰を下ろすと、のんびりした冷静な目で僕を見上げた。
lines.english: Then she settled quietly onto the round stool and looked up at me with placid, unhurried eyes.

lines.japanese: 「なに屋さんだと思ってたの？」
lines.english: “What kind of shop did you think it was?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ……煙草屋なんだけど……」
lines.english: “Well... a tobacco shop...”
“Mm... yes.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は訝しげに僕を凝視したまま、鈍重な亀のように時間をかけて頷いた。
lines.english: Still studying me with suspicion, she took all the time of a ponderous tortoise to nod.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、ちょっとね。考えごとしてたから、あはは、ぼけてた」
lines.english: “No, I was only... thinking about something. Ahaha. I was distracted.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君って思考障害の気があるの？」
lines.english: “Haneda, do you have some tendency toward disordered thinking?”

lines.japanese: 「そんな深刻な話にしないでよ……」
lines.english: “Please don't turn it into something that serious...”

lines.japanese: 「いい病院紹介しようか」
lines.english: “Would you like me to recommend a good hospital?”

lines.japanese: 「違うってば。それより山科さん、昨日と今日どうして学校──」
lines.english: “That's not what I meant. More importantly, Yamashina, why weren't you at school yesterday or—”

lines.japanese: 「そうだ、テストどうだった委員長？」
lines.english: “Oh, right. How did the exams go, class rep?”

lines.japanese: 「お、おれ？　おれは……まあ、ぼちぼちだけど」
lines.english: “M-me? I did… okay, I guess.”

lines.japanese: ちゃこん、と金属音がしたので横を見ると、セットアップの灰色スウェットを着込んだ中年男性が自販機にコインを入れていた。
lines.english: I heard a metallic clink and looked over. A middle-aged man in a matching gray sweatsuit was putting a coin into the vending machine.

lines.japanese: おじさんがボタンを押して煙草を拾いあげるまでのあいだ、僕はカウンターの下のガラスケースに並ぶパッケージへ視線を落としていた。
lines.english: While he pressed a button and retrieved his cigarettes, I lowered my gaze to the packages lined up in the glass case beneath the counter.

lines.japanese: 「それで、山科さんは学校どうしたの」
lines.english: “So what happened with school, Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: おじさんが立ちさる。僕は顔を上げた。
lines.english: The man walked away. I raised my head.

lines.japanese: 「テスト来てなかったけど、なんで？」
lines.english: “You missed the exams. Why?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、うん、ちょっと」
lines.english: “Oh. Mm. Something came up.”

lines.japanese: 「体調悪いの？」
lines.english: “Are you feeling sick?”

lines.japanese: 「んー？　んー」
lines.english: “Hmm? Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「え、病気？」
lines.english: “Are you ill?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、だいじょぶー」
lines.english: “Mm. I'm fine.”

lines.japanese: 僕の問いに対して山科さんは首を下に振ったが、そのまま正位置へは戻さなかった。まるで俯いてしまったみたいだ。
lines.english: Yamashina nodded at my question but didn't lift her head again. It looked like she'd simply dropped her gaze.

lines.japanese: カウンターの内側、彼女の落とした視線の先で携帯電話を開く音がした。えっ、なんでクラスメイトと話している最中に電話……？　まさか救急車？
lines.english: Behind the counter, somewhere beneath her lowered gaze, a cell phone snapped open. What? Why would she start making a call in the middle of talking to a classmate? Could she be calling an ambulance?

lines.japanese: 「うそ、ほんとに病気？　起きてていいの？　あっ、やば、もしかしておれが起こしちゃった？」
lines.english: “Wait, are you really sick? Should you even be up? Oh no—did I wake you?”

lines.japanese: 心配になってさらに尋ねると、ケータイを閉じる音と同時に山科さんが顔を上げた。手櫛で長い前髪を脇へ流して固定する。遮るもののなくなったふたつの瞳が、ちょっと驚いたみたいに丸く開かれていた。
lines.english: I got worried and asked again. Her phone clicked shut, and Yamashina looked up. She swept her long bangs to the side with her fingers and held them there. With nothing in the way, her eyes were wide, as if a little surprised.

lines.japanese: 「な、なに？」
lines.english: “W-what?”

lines.japanese: 「や、突きやぶってくるなーと思って」
lines.english: “Oh, I was just thinking you really do break straight through.”

lines.japanese: 手を放して唇の端で笑う。はらりと落ちた髪でふたたび顔半分が隠れた。
lines.english: She let her hand fall and smiled from one corner of her mouth. Her hair slipped down again, concealing half her face.
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「だって私、いまここに、こう──」
lines.english: “I mean, I had one right here, like this—”

lines.japanese: てのひらを横にして、目の上から顎の下までストンと一振り。
lines.english: She held her hand sideways and swept it straight down from above her eyes to beneath her chin.

lines.japanese: 「──見えなかった？」
lines.english: “—couldn't you see it?”

lines.japanese: 「何が？」
lines.english: “See what?”

lines.japanese: 「かべ」
lines.english: “A wall.”

lines.japanese: 「へっ？　なに？」
lines.english: “What? What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 彼女は上下の唇を薄く開けはなしたまま、ものも言わずにこちらを見上げる。女の子にじっと見詰められた僕は急に照れくさくなって、いそいそと視線を外した。
lines.english: Her lips remained slightly parted as she gazed up at me without a word. A girl was staring fixedly at me. I grew abruptly self-conscious and busied myself looking elsewhere.

lines.japanese: 「んー……いいか、べつに」
lines.english: “Hmm… Oh well. Never mind.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: つぶやき声が聞こえたので目を戻すと、山科さんは売り手側の低いテーブルに肘を置いて、さっきよりいくらかだけ身を乗りだしていた。
lines.english: I heard her murmur and looked back. Yamashina had propped her elbows on the low table behind the counter and leaned a little closer than before.

lines.japanese: 「あのね？　羽田君の質問に答えてもいいんだけど──」
lines.english: “Listen. I don't mind answering your question, Haneda, but—”

lines.japanese: 質問って……ああ、学校を休んだ理由か。すぐ答えてくれないから訊いた方が忘れてしまう。
lines.english: My question? Oh, why she had missed school. She had taken so long to answer that even the person who asked had forgotten.

lines.japanese: 「──面白くないわりに長くなるよ。先入観あると思うから、話すからには一言で片付けたくないし」
lines.english: “—it'll be a long answer for a boring story. You've probably got some preconceptions, and if I'm going to tell you, I don't want to just sum it up in one line.”

lines.japanese: 笑ってるときでさえ気だるげに淡々と流れるはずの彼女の声が、気のせいかな、なんだか今までより少しだけ弾んでるみたいに聞こえた。
lines.english: Even when she laughed, her voice ordinarily drifted on in the same languid monotone. Perhaps I imagined it, but now it seemed to carry the faintest lift.

lines.japanese: 「それでも聞いてくれるなら、はぐらかさないで今度はちゃんと答えるけど」
lines.english: “If you still want to hear it, I'll stop dodging and give you a proper answer this time.”

lines.japanese: 「今度はって。なにそれ、最初からちゃんと答えてよ」
lines.english: “What do you mean, this time? You should have answered properly from the start.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、やだ」
lines.english: “What? No.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんで」
lines.english: “W-why not?”

lines.japanese: 「軽々しく喧伝するようなことでもないし。それに挨拶程度の気遣いには、挨拶程度の対応をしてあげるのが相手のためでもあるでしょ」
lines.english: “It isn’t something to broadcast lightly. Besides, if someone offers no more than passing concern, answering with no more than a passing response is kinder to them too.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: どうにも分かりにくい。やけに持って回った言い方をするのは癖なんだろうか。僕は困惑を微笑で上書きして訊いた。
lines.english: It was hard to follow. Was talking in these roundabout ways just a habit of hers? I hid my confusion behind a smile and asked again.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃもう一回聞くけど、なんで今日は学校休んだの」
lines.english: “Then I'll ask one more time. Why did you miss school today?”

lines.japanese: 「なんで。んー、メカニズムとしては……」
lines.english: “Why? Hmm. In terms of the mechanism...”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは噛みつぶすように疑問詞を復唱したあと、視線を落としてしばし言葉を選ぶような顔になった。
lines.english: Yamashina repeated the question word as though chewing it apart. Then she lowered her eyes and seemed to spend a moment selecting her words.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、自律神経って知ってる？」
lines.english: “Haneda, do you know what the autonomic nervous system is?”

lines.japanese: いきなり医学書っぽい言葉が出てきた。
lines.english: Out of nowhere came a phrase straight from a medical textbook.

lines.japanese: 「はあ……いや、名前ぐらいなら……」
lines.english: “Well... I've heard the name...”

lines.japanese: 自信なさげな答えしか返せなかったけど、彼女もそれを予期していたようだ。だよね、という表情で小さく頷いた。
lines.english: It was the best answer I could give, and not a confident one, but she appeared to have expected it. She gave a small nod that said, Of course.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ大雑把に言うけど、自律神経には交感神経っていうのと副交感神経っていうのがあるのね。普段はだいたい、このふたつが平衡を保ってると思って？」
lines.english: “Then I'll be very general. The autonomic nervous system has two parts: the sympathetic and the parasympathetic nervous systems. Ordinarily, you can think of those two as remaining in balance.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんはうつ伏せたてのひらを左右に並べて、天秤の皿みたいにゆらゆら上下させた。それを僕は小窓越しに覗きこんでいた。
lines.english: Yamashina laid both hands facedown beside each other and rocked them gently up and down like the pans of a scale. I watched through the little window.

lines.japanese: 「たとえば大事な試験とか試合の前って、どきどきしたり、そわそわしたり、がちがちになったりするでしょ。あれは交感神経が優位に立ってる状態」
lines.english: “Before an important exam or a match, for example, your heart pounds, you feel restless, your whole body goes rigid. That's the sympathetic nervous system becoming dominant.”

lines.japanese: と言いながら天秤の右を上げ、左を下げる。
lines.english: As she spoke, she raised the right side of her scale and lowered the left.

lines.japanese: 「狩猟時代の名残なのかな。心拍数上げたり筋肉硬くしたりして、戦いに備えるんだよね……適度の緊張は意欲を上げるし、体の動きも良くなるでしょ。あ、あとアドレナリンが分泌されるから痛みにも強くなるらしいよ」
lines.english: “Maybe it's left over from our hunting days. Your heart speeds up and your muscles tense so you're ready to fight... A little tension makes you more motivated and helps your body move better, right? Oh, and since it releases adrenaline, apparently you can take more pain too.”

lines.japanese: 「で逆に、お風呂とかご飯のあとなんかは、まったりーとして、うとうとしてくるよね。あれは副交感神経が優位に立ってる状態」
lines.english: “On the other hand, after a bath or a meal, you get all relaxed and sleepy, right? That's when the parasympathetic nervous system has the upper hand.”

lines.japanese: 今度は天秤の位置を左右真逆にする。
lines.english: This time she reversed the positions of the scale.

lines.japanese: 「血行を良くしたり筋肉をリラックスさせたりして、体から怪我とか疲れを取りのぞこうっていう状態ね。たとえば体調を崩すとだるくて気力がなくなるのは、体が癒しを求めて副交感神経を優位にしてるからなの」
lines.english: “It gets your blood flowing, relaxes your muscles, and puts your body in recovery mode so it can heal injuries and fatigue. Like, when you're sick and feel wiped out and can't get motivated, that's because your body wants to heal, so it puts your parasympathetic nervous system in charge.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ……戦闘モードと回復モードってわけだ」
lines.english: “I see... Battle mode and recovery mode.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね」
lines.english: “That's right.”

lines.japanese: 我ながら男子的な比喩だなあと思ったけど、山科さんは面白そうに笑ってくれた。
lines.english: It struck me as a thoroughly boyish analogy, but Yamashina smiled as though she liked it.

lines.japanese: 「普通の人間の体って、そこのところの均衡がうまく調整されるようになっててー。普段はこう、バランスよく中立あたりを保ちつつね？　必要に応じて、しゃっきりさせたり、まったりさせたりって」
lines.english: “So, a normal person's body is set up to keep that balance working right. Usually it stays somewhere around neutral, nice and balanced, you know? Then when it needs to, it either perks you up or chills you out.”

lines.japanese: 落ちついて淡々と語りながらも、伸ばした両手をふよふよ上下させる山科さんはちょっと可愛かった。
lines.english: Even as she explained in her usual composed monotone, Yamashina's two outstretched hands bobbed dreamily up and down. It was rather endearing.

lines.japanese: 「で話は戻るんだけど、私いま厄介な病気のせいで、そのバランス機能に異状を来たしててー」
lines.english: “Anyway, back to what I was saying. This annoying illness I have is messing up that whole balancing thing—”
“What?!”

lines.japanese: 突然の閑話休題、しかも「厄介な病気」やら「異状を来たした」やらの不吉な言葉に動転した僕は、慌てて確認しようと彼女の体をてっぺんから下へ向けて──
lines.english: The abrupt return to the subject—and ominous phrases like “troublesome illness” and “disrupted function”—threw me into a panic. I hurriedly examined her from the top of her head downward—

lines.japanese: 「肉眼じゃ見えないと思うよ、神経は」
lines.english: “I don't think you can see nerves with the naked eye.”

lines.japanese: ──目の動きだけで心を読まれてしまった。
lines.english: —and she read my mind from the movement of my eyes alone.

lines.japanese: 「そっ、それで？　その、異状を来たすっていうのはどういう……」
lines.english: “Th-then what happens? What does it mean for the function to be disrupted?”

lines.japanese: 「天秤が故障してるってことかな。針があんまり平衡に戻ってくれなくて、副交感神経に偏りがちなの」
lines.english: “I suppose it means the scale is broken. The needle doesn't like to return to equilibrium, and it tends to remain tipped toward the parasympathetic side.”

lines.japanese: 副交感……っていうと、ええと、まったりモードの方か。
lines.english: Parasympathetic... That was the mellow mode, if I remembered correctly.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、風呂あがりのほわーっとしたのがずっと続いてるってこと？」
lines.english: “So it's like that warm, floaty feeling after a bath, except it never ends?”

lines.japanese: 「そんないいものじゃないよ」
lines.english: “It isn't anything that pleasant.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは困り笑いを浮かべながら首を横に振った。
lines.english: Yamashina shook her head with a troubled smile.

lines.japanese: 「もっとね、体がずーんと重くて、頭がもやーっと曇ってて……」
lines.english: “My body feels leaden, and my mind is buried in fog…”

lines.japanese: 「んー、思うように動けないって言うか、動かせるような気がしないって言うか、なんだろ、自分が自分じゃない感じっていうのかな」
lines.english: “Hmm. I can’t move the way I want—or rather, I don’t feel as though I can make myself move. How can I put it? I don’t feel like myself.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、熱があるときのふらふらするみたいな」
lines.english: “Oh. Like when a fever makes you dizzy?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、悪寒とか倦怠感っていうのとは微妙に違う感覚なんだ。なんだろ、ええと──」
lines.english: “No, it's not quite the same as chills or feeling wiped out. It's... how do I put it? Um—”

lines.japanese: 「──たとえば自分の失敗で、誰か他のひとに迷惑をかけちゃったと思って」
lines.english: “—suppose you made a mistake and caused trouble for someone else.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “R-right.”

lines.japanese: とりあえず頷いたものの、いきなりそんなことを言われても想像力は働かない。そんな生返事が効いたのか、山科さんは一瞬考えてから補足する。
lines.english: I nodded for now, but hearing that out of nowhere, I couldn't really picture it. Maybe my halfhearted answer tipped her off, because Yamashina thought for a moment and added:

lines.japanese: 「間違った英文訳を教えたせいで、隣りの席の子に恥をかかせちゃったとか。バイト先で大きいミスをして、みんなを残業に巻きこんじゃったとか。そういう経験ない？」
lines.english: “Maybe you gave the student beside you the wrong translation of an English sentence and embarrassed them. Or made a huge mistake at work and forced everyone to stay late. Has anything like that ever happened to you?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いや、そういうことなら……」
lines.english: “Oh. If that's what you mean...”

lines.japanese: あったと思う。いくらでも。
lines.english: It had. More times than I could count.

lines.japanese: 「そういうときって、なんとも言えないヤな気分になるでしょ。ホームで帰りの電車を待ってても、家で布団を被ってても、はぁーって溜息ばっかり出てきて」
lines.english: “At times like that, you feel awful in a way you can't put into words. You stand on the platform waiting for your train home, or lie in bed with the covers over your head, and all you can do is sigh.”

lines.japanese: 「なんであんなことしちゃったんだろ、なんて役に立たないやつなんだろって、どんどん暗い気分になってって、もう自分に向かって消えろよ無能とか思うでしょ」
lines.english: “Why did I do that? How can I be so useless? The darkness keeps gathering until you're telling yourself to disappear, you worthless idiot.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんの自虐的な冗談に愛想笑いを挿むのも忘れて、僕は操られるように頷いていた。
lines.english: I forgot even to supply the polite laugh her self-mocking joke required. I was nodding as though she controlled me.

lines.japanese: 「うん……分かる……」
lines.english: “Yes... I know what you mean...”

lines.japanese: 「ほんと？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「いなくなりたい、って、思うよね」
lines.english: “You want to disappear, don’t you.”

lines.japanese: よろしくグレタガルド。
lines.english: Hello, Gretagard.

lines.japanese: 「思うよねー」
lines.english: “You really do.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は唸るようにしみじみ同意した。嬉しそうだ。僕は空を仰いだ。都会の夜には星が見えなかった。
lines.english: She agreed with a heartfelt murmur. She looked pleased. I gazed up at the sky. In the city night, there were no stars.

lines.japanese: 「例えるなら、そういうどんよりした最低の気分がわけもなくずーっと続いてる感じ。かな？」
lines.english: “So imagine that same heavy, miserable feeling going on and on, for no reason at all. That's about what it's like.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは「天秤が故障している状態」をそう説明した。
lines.english: That was how Yamashina explained “a broken scale.”

lines.japanese: 「故障って言っても完全に止まっちゃったわけじゃなくて、いちおう偏ってる範囲内でのアップダウンはあるんだけど。でも困ったことに、これがまた時と場合を選んでくれなくて」
lines.english: “Broken doesn't mean it has stopped completely. There are still ups and downs within the range where it's stuck. The trouble is, those changes pay no attention whatsoever to time or circumstance.”

lines.japanese: 「だから今日も朝、出掛けに大っきい波が来ちゃって。ダウンの。ちょっと外に出られる状態じゃなかった」
lines.english: “So this morning, right as I was heading out, a huge wave hit. A down one. I really couldn't go outside like that.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうだったんだ……」
lines.english: “Oh. I see...”

lines.japanese: 今朝の彼女を思いだしてみる。僕と話してるあいだは辛そうな感じじゃなかった。ていうことは、あの直後に発作が起きたんだろう。
lines.english: I tried to remember her that morning. She had not seemed to be suffering while she spoke with me. The attack must have come immediately afterward.

lines.japanese: 「あ……それで、いまは平気なの？」
lines.english: “And... are you all right now?”

lines.japanese: 「いまはわりと上がってる方。だから普通に話せてる……え、私いま普通に話せてるよね？」
lines.english: “I'm actually doing pretty well right now. That's why I can talk normally... Wait, I am talking normally right now, aren't I?”

lines.japanese: 「なにが？　普通に話せないときがあるの？」
lines.english: “What do you mean? Are there times when you can't?”

lines.japanese: 「あ……あー、うん、まあ」
lines.english: “Oh... Ah. Yes, I suppose.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、どんな風に」
lines.english: “Really? What are you like?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、まー、いろいろ」
lines.english: “Oh, you know. Various things.”

lines.japanese: 「いろいろって？」
lines.english: “What things?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ちょっと」
lines.english: “Well. It's complicated.”

lines.japanese: と言って彼女は手の甲を横にしてこちらへ向け、目の上から顎の下まで、シャッターでも下ろすみたいに一閃させた。
lines.english: She turned the back of her hand toward me and swept it down from above her eyes to beneath her chin, like a shutter falling.
“...Excuse me?”

lines.japanese: 「おしまい」
lines.english: “The end.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なんで、話まだ途中──」
lines.english: “What? Why? You were still—”

lines.japanese: 「おしまい」
lines.english: “The end.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、そんな、ずるいよ。気になるじゃん、ちゃんと最後まで──」
lines.english: “That's not fair. Now I want to know. At least finish what you—”

lines.japanese: 僕が首を突きだすと、山科さんは目を伏せて大きく息を吸いこんだ。
lines.english: When I craned my neck closer, Yamashina lowered her eyes and drew a deep breath.

lines.japanese: 「踏みこんでくるなあっ」
lines.english: “You really do come barging straight in!”

lines.japanese: かすれた声で一言呟くと、親指の爪をかりかりと前歯で弾きだした。
lines.english: She muttered the words hoarsely, then began worrying at her thumbnail with her front teeth.
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 空気の変化を感じて、僕は思わず体を引いた。
lines.english: I felt the air change and instinctively drew back.

lines.japanese: 「喋りすぎたごめん、いま言ったのぜんぶ忘れて。変な目で見られたくないから」
lines.english: “I said too much—sorry. Forget everything I just told you. I don't want you looking at me like I'm strange.”

lines.japanese: 「変なって……なんで、どうしたの急に。全然そんな、思わないよ」
lines.english: “Strange? Why would I? What happened all of a sudden? I don't think anything like that.”

lines.japanese: 「みんな最初はそう言う」
lines.english: “Everyone says that at first.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、べつに最初だけじゃ……」
lines.english: “No, not just at first…”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、そう言うの」
lines.english: “Yes. They say that too.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、おれは違うよ」
lines.english: “But I'm different.”

lines.japanese: 「それも言うなあ」
lines.english: “They say that as well.”

lines.japanese: 「でも」
lines.english: “But—”

lines.japanese: 「もういいよ、黙れよほんと！」
lines.english: “Enough. Just shut up already!”

lines.japanese: 仔ウサギの歯みたいな牽制だった。予期せぬ一撃に僕は息を呑む。いま鏡を見れば、きっとひどく強張った顔をしていることだろう。
lines.english: It was a warning nip from the teeth of a baby rabbit. The unexpected blow made me catch my breath. If I could have seen myself in a mirror, my face would surely have been rigid with shock.

lines.japanese: でも次の瞬間──
lines.english: But in the next instant—
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: ──山科さんの表情も固まっていた。丸く見開かれた瞳の中で光沢が揺れ、雫となってこぼれそうだった。
lines.english: —I saw that Yamashina's expression had frozen too. Light trembled in her round, wide eyes, threatening to spill over in drops.

lines.japanese: 「あは。なんてね。びっくりした？」
lines.english: “Ahaha. Just kidding. Did I scare you?”

lines.japanese: そして彼女は表情を隠し、繕うように笑った。俯いて口元を手で覆うさまは、なんだかはみ出てしまった線を消しゴムで消そうとしてるみたいだった。
lines.english: Then she hid her expression and gave a laugh to smooth things over. Head bowed, hand covering her mouth, she looked as though she were trying to erase a line that had strayed outside the drawing.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、べつに……」
lines.english: “Oh, no. It's nothing...”

lines.japanese: しどろもどろに答えながら僕も笑った。山科さんは頭を奥の障子戸へ向けたまま、作ったような明るい声で言った。
lines.english: I laughed too as I fumbled for an answer. Yamashina kept her face turned toward the screen door behind her and spoke with an artificial brightness.

lines.japanese: 「やだな。やっぱり普通に話せなかった。ふられるわけだよね」
lines.english: “How awful. I couldn't talk normally after all. No wonder I got dumped.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 「ごめん私、薬飲んでくる。じゃあね」
lines.english: “Sorry. I need to take my medicine. See you.”

lines.japanese: そして僕の顔も見ずにいきなり立ちあがった。
lines.english: She stood abruptly without once looking at my face.

lines.japanese: そのまま駆けだしそうな勢いだったけど、でも、とつぜん立ち眩みしたみたいにフラッと一回横に傾いた。
lines.english: She seemed ready to break into a run, but suddenly swayed sideways as though overcome by dizziness.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっ……大丈夫！？」
lines.english: “Wait—are you all right!?”

lines.japanese: 頼りない背中はそう答えたあと、しかし進みもせず戻りもせず、土間の真ん中に呆然と立ちつくしていた。
lines.english: Her frail back gave me that answer, but then she neither went forward nor came back. She simply stood in the middle of the earthen floor, lost.

lines.japanese: 「ど、どうしたの……」
lines.english: “W-what's wrong...?”

lines.japanese: 不思議に思って声をかけた。答えはなかったけど、代わりに彼女は背筋を曲げて、頭をぐんにゃり前へと傾けた。
lines.english: Puzzled, I called to her. She did not answer. Instead, her spine bent and her head sagged limply forward.

lines.japanese: 「あの、山科さん……？」
lines.english: “Um... Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: ようやく彼女は、長い前髪をぐずぐず引っぱりながら、猫背気味の姿勢で振りかえった。眠たげに半分塞がりかけた幽霊みたいな目は、一瞬あさっての方向へさまよいかけたのちに僕を見つける。
lines.english: At last she turned, tugging fretfully at her long bangs, shoulders hunched. Her ghostlike eyes, drooping sleepily half shut, wandered off in the wrong direction before finding me.

lines.japanese: 「……あの……この話……あんまり広めないでもらえると助かる……」
lines.english: “...Um... It would help if you didn't tell too many people about this...”

lines.japanese: 「え……うん」
lines.english: “Oh... All right.”

lines.japanese: 「ほら……なんか……うそっぽいし……きもいでしょ……」
lines.english: “I mean… it sounds made-up… and creepy, doesn’t it…?”

lines.japanese: うつろな目でぼそぼそと呟く。聞きとりにくくてワンテンポ遅れてしまったけれど、僕はたしかに頷いた。
lines.english: She mumbled with vacant eyes. I couldn't quite make out the words, so I was a beat late, but I did nod.

lines.japanese: 「分かった。言わないよ、誰にも」
lines.english: “I understand. I won't tell anyone.”

lines.japanese: どうせ言うような相手もいない。
lines.english: It's not like I had anyone to tell anyway.

lines.japanese: 彼女はひどく億劫そうに微笑んで、ほとんど唇を動かすことなく囁いた。
lines.english: She smiled as though even that small effort cost her dearly, and whispered with scarcely a movement of her lips.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん……ありがと……」
lines.english: “Sorry... Thank you...”

lines.japanese: なんだか立ってるのが辛そうだ。これが例の「波」ってやつなのかもしれない。
lines.english: Even standing appeared painful. Perhaps this was one of the “waves” she had described.

lines.japanese: 「学校、明日は来られそう？」
lines.english: “Do you think you can come to school tomorrow?”

lines.japanese: 尋ねると、山科さんは弱々しい笑顔を小さく傾けた。
lines.english: At the question, Yamashina tipped her faint smile to one side.

lines.japanese: 「……分かんない……明日になってみないと……」
lines.english: “...I don't know... I won't know until tomorrow...”

lines.japanese: そして最後に、顔の横で右手をぱっくんぱっくんと開閉させてから、体を引きずるように歩いていった。
lines.english: Finally she opened and closed her right hand beside her face like a little mouth, then dragged herself away.

lines.japanese: 彼女が無事に座敷へ辿りつくのを見届けてから、僕は煙草屋をあとにした。
lines.english: I waited until she had safely reached the sitting room before leaving the tobacco shop.

lines.japanese: 寒空の下に立っていたせいで体が冷えこんでいる。かじかんだ指先に白い息を吹きつけた。
lines.english: Standing beneath the cold sky had chilled me through. I blew white breath over my numb fingertips.

lines.japanese: 寝静まった住宅街をひとり歩いていると、ふと、自分は普通に話せているかと聞いた山科さんの真面目な顔が思いだされた。
lines.english: As I walked alone through the sleeping residential streets, I suddenly remembered Yamashina's solemn face when she had asked whether she was speaking normally.

lines.japanese: そんな判定が僕に下せるはずはない。むしろこっちが聞きたいぐらいだ。
lines.english: There was no way I could judge that. If anything, I was the one who wanted to ask.

lines.japanese: 羽田の家までの道すがら、退屈しのぎに携帯電話からインターネットに繋げた。
lines.english: On the way to the Haneda house, I got bored and went online on my phone.

lines.japanese: 耳慣れない日本語や外来語に遭遇したときしばしばそうするように、僕は山科さんの口にのぼった印象的な単語をいくつか検索エンジンにかけてみた。
lines.english: As I often did when I encountered unfamiliar Japanese or foreign terminology, I entered several memorable words from Yamashina's explanation into a search engine.

lines.japanese: そうしたら、うつ病とか精神疾患とか心療内科とかに関するページがたくさん引っかかって、僕は無意識に歩く速度を落としていた。
lines.english: That brought up tons of pages about depression, mental illness, psychosomatic medicine, and so on. Without realizing it, I'd started walking more slowly.

lines.japanese: そういえば山科さんは、病状の説明を求められて、最初はぐらかすように口ごもっていた。なのに僕は、彼女が下ろしたシャッターを臆面もなく突きやぶって踏みこんでしまったんだ。
lines.english: Come to think of it, when I asked Yamashina about her condition, she had faltered and tried at first to evade the question. Yet I had shamelessly smashed through the shutter she lowered and barged inside.

lines.japanese: そのままケータイを畳んでポケットに押しこんだ。僕はなんて空気の読めないやつなんだろう。なんて役に立たないやつなんだろう。
lines.english: I folded the phone shut and shoved it into my pocket. I really couldn't read the room. I really was useless.

lines.japanese: 山科さんの言葉を借りて、自分に放つ。
lines.english: I borrowed Yamashina's words and turned them upon myself.

lines.japanese: 「消えろよ無能」
lines.english: “Disappear, you worthless idiot.”
